bridge-type.label: EEBus OH Device
bridge-type.description: One local EEBus SHIP/SPINE service instance (own certificate, mDNS presence).

parameter.name: deviceType
parameter.label: Device Type
parameter.description: Which SPINE Device type this Bridge's local SHIP/SPINE service instance presents itself as in detailed discovery (docs/ADR/044-configurable-devicetype.md). Independent of the entityType configured on attached oh-...-entity children (docs/ADR/042-configurable-entitytype.md) - deviceType classifies the Device as a whole, entityType classifies the one shared local Entity; jeebus.spine's own Use-Case entity-type check never looks at this value. Safe to leave at the default unless you have a specific reason to present this service as a different SPINE device type.

parameter.name: vendorCode
parameter.label: Vendor Code
parameter.description: 5-character vendor code assigned by the EEBUS Initiative. Part of the SHIP-ID: pinned at first start, later changes are ignored (would break existing pairings).

parameter.name: deviceBrand
parameter.label: Device Brand
parameter.description: Brand / manufacturer name, announced via mDNS.

parameter.name: deviceModel
parameter.label: Device Model
parameter.description: Model name, announced via mDNS. Part of the SHIP-ID: pinned at first start, later changes are ignored (would break existing pairings).

parameter.name: serialNumber
parameter.label: Serial Number
parameter.description: Serial number, used together with vendor code/model to build the SHIP-ID. Pinned at first start, later changes are ignored (would break existing pairings).

parameter.name: mdnsServiceInstance
parameter.label: Display Name
parameter.description: Friendly name other EEBUS devices see when they discover this service, e.g. "openHAB EnergyManager".

parameter.name: port
parameter.label: Port
parameter.description: WebSocket port the local SHIP server listens on. Leave empty to have openHAB assign a free port automatically (4711-4810).

parameter.name: trustedSkis
parameter.label: Trusted SKIs
parameter.description: Subject Key Identifiers (40 hex characters each) this Bridge trusts as SHIP Nodes - the source of truth for which devices it accepts/dials. Offered as a selectable list of known hw-device Things and other local Bridges' own SKIs (docs/ADR/024-oh-device-oh-entity-rename.md) - free text entry remains possible for a SKI not yet seen. Editing this list triggers a full rebuild of this Bridge's local SPINE service, automatically, briefly reconnecting every currently trusted peer - see docs/ADR/027-derive-local-use-cases-from-entities.md.

parameter.name: connectToPeers
parameter.label: Actively Connect to Trusted Peers
parameter.description: If enabled (default), this service actively dials trusted peers as soon as they are discovered via mDNS, in addition to accepting their incoming connections - this is the normal SHIP behavior, where either side may initiate. Disable only as a diagnostic workaround when pairing two self-built openHAB instances against each other: with both sides actively dialing, they can connect to each other at the same moment, and a known bug in the embedded SHIP library's simultaneous-connection handling can then abort the handshake (see TEST_PAIRING.md, Test 2, "Known Bug Encountered"). Disabling this on one of the two sides makes that side purely passive (server-only) and avoids the race. Not recommended against a real third-party device, which may rely on openHAB dialing out.

parameter.name: preferIpv4
parameter.label: Prefer IPv4 for own SHIP server
parameter.description: If enabled (default), binds/announces the local SHIP server on IPv4 instead of the IPv6-first preference the single-address fix would otherwise use. Recommended standard setting: works around a confirmed bug in the embedded SHIP library when reconnecting to an IPv6 peer (missing "[...]" brackets around the IPv6 host, observed as "connect to null on port -1" followed by a timed-out SPINE request) - confirmed via a live A/B comparison on 2026-08-21, see EEBusConfiguration#preferIpv4. Disable to return to the IPv6-first preference, e.g. to re-test after an upstream fix in the embedded SHIP library.

thing-type.label: EEBus Hardware Device
thing-type.description: A real EEBus device seen on the network, identified by its SKI. Not trusted - see eebus:oh-entity for representing a SPINE Entity on a device trusted by a local EEBus OH Device. CONCEPT.md's 2026-08-23 addendum.

parameter.name: ski
parameter.label: SKI
parameter.description: Subject Key Identifier of the remote device (40 hex characters), e.g. read from its display or QR code.

thing-type.label: EEBus OH Entity
thing-type.description: One SPINE Entity on a device trusted by the parent eebus:oh-device Bridge, identified by the device's SKI and this Entity's address. Trust itself is granted/revoked on the parent Bridge's Trusted SKIs config list - configuring this Thing alone does not grant trust. Which Use Cases this pairing involves is configured below and feeds directly into the parent Bridge's local SPINE service - see docs/ADR/027-derive-local-use-cases-from-entities.md.

parameter.name: ski
parameter.label: Device SKI
parameter.description: Subject Key Identifier of the remote device this Entity lives on (40 hex characters). Optional - left blank, it is auto-selected once the parent Bridge trusts exactly one device (nothing to choose between); with zero or more than one trusted device, pick one manually. Offered as a selectable list of the parent Bridge's currently trusted SKIs (docs/ADR/024-oh-device-oh-entity-rename.md) - free text entry remains possible for a SKI not yet trusted, but this Thing stays offline until the parent Bridge actually trusts it (see the Bridge's Trusted SKIs config).

parameter.name: entityAddress
parameter.label: Entity Address
parameter.description: SPINE address of this Entity on the device (as shown by device discovery/NodeManagement data). Recorded for reference; not yet used to route data at the transport layer - a device with more than one Entity Thing configured currently has all of them observe the same device-level events. See docs/ADR/024-oh-device-oh-entity-rename.md "Out of scope".

parameter.name: shipId
parameter.label: SHIP ID
parameter.description: Learned automatically during the first successful handshake - normally left empty.

parameter.name: entityType
parameter.label: Entity Type
parameter.description: Which SPINE Entity type this Entity is presented as.

parameter.description: Which EEBUS use cases openHAB should try to detect/consume on trusted devices. See CONCEPT.md §5.4.1. Wiring is not yet implemented - see CONCEPT.md §7 items 3+8.

thing-type.label: EEBus OH Energy Guard Entity
thing-type.description: One SPINE Entity on a device trusted by the parent eebus:oh-device Bridge, identified by the device's SKI and this Entity's address - alternative to eebus:oh-entity for the EnergyGuard (LPC/LPP Client role) case. Its mere presence makes the parent Bridge offer LPC+LPP Client - values flow only via a tagged Item's write path (see README.md "Channels"), this Thing has no Channels of its own. Trust itself is granted/revoked on the parent Bridge's Trusted SKIs config list - configuring this Thing alone does not grant trust. See docs/ADR/027-derive-local-use-cases-from-entities.md and docs/ADR/031-remove-energyguard-monitoring-channels.md. As of docs/ADR/047-fanout-energyguard-writes-to-all-partners.md, exactly one oh-eg-entity Thing per parent Bridge is the supported configuration - its write path feeds every trusted partner the Bridge's EnergyGuard use cases find, not just one.

parameter.name: ski
parameter.label: Device SKI
parameter.description: Leave blank (recommended, docs/ADR/047-fanout-energyguard-writes-to-all-partners.md): this Thing's write-path Items are then sent to every partner the parent Bridge's EnergyGuard use cases currently find, whatever device SKI each one lives on - this is the setting for the normal case of one EnergyGuard feeding several controllable peers (e.g. an inverter, evcc, and this binding's own Controllable System entity) with the same limit. Set to one specific 40-hex-character SKI only to restrict this Thing to that single partner and exclude every other trusted device - a narrower, less common case than the pre-ADR-047 default. Offered as a selectable list of the parent Bridge's currently trusted SKIs (docs/ADR/024-oh-device-oh-entity-rename.md) - free text entry remains possible for a SKI not yet trusted, but the restriction only takes effect once the parent Bridge actually trusts it (see the Bridge's Trusted SKIs config). Configuring more than one oh-eg-entity Thing under the same Bridge is not a supported configuration going forward (ADR-047) - existing multi-Thing setups keep working, but only the first oh-eg-entity Thing found actually drives the write path; consolidate to a single Thing with a blank ski instead.

parameter.name: entityAddress
parameter.label: Entity Address
parameter.description: SPINE address of this Entity on the device (as shown by device discovery/NodeManagement data). Recorded for reference; not yet used to route data at the transport layer - a device with more than one Entity Thing configured currently has all of them observe the same device-level events. See docs/ADR/024-oh-device-oh-entity-rename.md "Out of scope".

parameter.name: shipId
parameter.label: SHIP ID
parameter.description: Learned automatically during the first successful handshake - normally left empty.

parameter.name: entityType
parameter.label: Entity Type
parameter.description: Which SPINE Entity type this Energy Guard is presented as.

thing-type.label: EEBus OH Controllable System Entity
thing-type.description: One SPINE Entity on a device trusted by the parent eebus:oh-device Bridge, identified by the device's SKI and this Entity's address. Trust itself is granted/revoked on the parent Bridge's Trusted SKIs config list - configuring this Thing alone does not grant trust. Its mere presence makes the parent Bridge offer LPC+LPP Server, seeded from the failsafe values below - its lpc/lpp Channels (limit-active, limit-value, failsafe-limit-value, failsafe-duration-minimum) are present from the start. See docs/ADR/027-derive-local-use-cases-from-entities.md.

parameter.name: ski
parameter.label: Device SKI
parameter.description: Subject Key Identifier of the remote device this Entity lives on (40 hex characters). Optional - left blank, it is auto-selected once the parent Bridge trusts exactly one device (nothing to choose between); with zero or more than one trusted device, pick one manually. Offered as a selectable list of the parent Bridge's currently trusted SKIs (docs/ADR/024-oh-device-oh-entity-rename.md) - free text entry remains possible for a SKI not yet trusted, but this Thing stays offline until the parent Bridge actually trusts it (see the Bridge's Trusted SKIs config).

parameter.name: entityAddress
parameter.label: Entity Address
parameter.description: SPINE address of this Entity on the device (as shown by device discovery/NodeManagement data). Recorded for reference; not yet used to route data at the transport layer - a device with more than one Entity Thing configured currently has all of them observe the same device-level events. See docs/ADR/024-oh-device-oh-entity-rename.md "Out of scope".

parameter.name: shipId
parameter.label: SHIP ID
parameter.description: Learned automatically during the first successful handshake - normally left empty.

parameter.name: entityType
parameter.label: Entity Type
parameter.description: Which SPINE Entity type this Controllable System is presented as.

parameter.name: failsafeConsumptionLimitSeedWatts
parameter.label: Failsafe Consumption Limit (Seed)
parameter.description: The power limit value (Watts) this Controllable System presents for LPC (Limitation of Power Consumption) at every startup, until a paired Energy Guard writes a different value over EEBus. Not editable from openHAB after startup except by adding/re-adding this Thing - only the Energy Guard, over EEBus, changes the running value. See docs/ADR/023-cs-service-convenience-bridge.md.

parameter.name: failsafeProductionLimitSeedWatts
parameter.label: Failsafe Production Limit (Seed)
parameter.description: Same as Failsafe Consumption Limit (Seed), for LPP (Limitation of Power Production).

parameter.name: failsafeDurationMinimumSeedSeconds
parameter.label: Failsafe Duration Minimum (Seed)
parameter.description: The minimum duration (seconds) the failsafe limit is presented as remaining in effect, shared by LPC and LPP, at every startup - until a paired Energy Guard writes a different value over EEBus. Same not-editable-at-runtime-from-openHAB rule as the limit seeds above.

thing-type.label: EEBus OH Monitoring Entity
thing-type.description: One SPINE Entity on a device trusted by the parent eebus:oh-device Bridge, dedicated to reading its power/energy/current/voltage/frequency measurements (MPC). Trust is granted on the parent Bridge's Trusted SKIs list - configuring this Thing alone does not grant trust. Its mere presence makes the parent Bridge offer MPC Client; its mpc Channels are present from the start.

parameter.name: ski
parameter.label: Device SKI
parameter.description: Subject Key Identifier of the remote device this Entity lives on (40 hex characters). Optional if the parent Bridge trusts exactly one device; otherwise pick one from the trusted list.

parameter.name: entityAddress
parameter.label: Entity Address
parameter.description: SPINE address of this Entity on the device. For reference only; not yet used to route data.

parameter.name: shipId
parameter.label: SHIP ID
parameter.description: Learned automatically during the first successful handshake - normally left empty.

parameter.name: entityType
parameter.label: Entity Type
parameter.description: Which SPINE Entity type this Entity is presented as.

channel-group-type.label: MPC (Monitoring of Power Consumption)
channel-group-type.description: Client-role data read from a trusted device's Entity offering MPC as a Server actor. Appears once MPC is detected for this Entity - see docs/ADR/014-dynamic-client-role-channels.md.

channel-type.label: Power
channel-type.description: Total active power currently consumed/produced by the Entity, per MPC Scenario 1 (Total Active Power, [MPC-011]) - see CONCEPT.md §5.4.3.

channel-type.label: Power (Phase A)
channel-type.description: Active power on phase A currently consumed/produced by the Entity, per MPC Scenario 1 (Phase-Specific Active Power, [MPC-012/1]) - see CONCEPT.md §5.4.3.

channel-type.label: Power (Phase B)
channel-type.description: Active power on phase B currently consumed/produced by the Entity, per MPC Scenario 1 (Phase-Specific Active Power, [MPC-012/2]) - see CONCEPT.md §5.4.3.

channel-type.label: Power (Phase C)
channel-type.description: Active power on phase C currently consumed/produced by the Entity, per MPC Scenario 1 (Phase-Specific Active Power, [MPC-012/3]) - see CONCEPT.md §5.4.3.

channel-type.label: Energy Consumed
channel-type.description: Total energy consumed by the Entity, per MPC Scenario 2 (Total Consumed Energy, [MPC-021]) - see CONCEPT.md §5.4.3.

channel-type.label: Energy Produced
channel-type.description: Total energy produced by the Entity, per MPC Scenario 2 (Total Produced Energy, [MPC-022]) - see CONCEPT.md §5.4.3.

channel-type.label: Current (Phase A)
channel-type.description: AC current on phase A, per MPC Scenario 3 (Phase-Specific AC Current, [MPC-031/1]) - see CONCEPT.md §5.4.3.

channel-type.label: Current (Phase B)
channel-type.description: AC current on phase B, per MPC Scenario 3 (Phase-Specific AC Current, [MPC-031/2]) - see CONCEPT.md §5.4.3.

channel-type.label: Current (Phase C)
channel-type.description: AC current on phase C, per MPC Scenario 3 (Phase-Specific AC Current, [MPC-031/3]) - see CONCEPT.md §5.4.3.

channel-type.label: Voltage (Phase A-Neutral)
channel-type.description: AC voltage between phase A and neutral, per MPC Scenario 4 (AC Voltage Phase-Neutral, [MPC-041/1]) - see CONCEPT.md §5.4.3.

channel-type.label: Voltage (Phase B-Neutral)
channel-type.description: AC voltage between phase B and neutral, per MPC Scenario 4 (AC Voltage Phase-Neutral, [MPC-041/2]) - see CONCEPT.md §5.4.3.

channel-type.label: Voltage (Phase C-Neutral)
channel-type.description: AC voltage between phase C and neutral, per MPC Scenario 4 (AC Voltage Phase-Neutral, [MPC-041/3]) - see CONCEPT.md §5.4.3.

channel-type.label: Voltage (Phase A-B)
channel-type.description: AC voltage between phases A-B, per MPC Scenario 4 (AC Voltage Phase-Phase, [MPC-041/4]) - see CONCEPT.md §5.4.3. Not populated by this binding: no distinct measurement identifier is available to resolve it (docs/ADR/037-mpc-additional- datapoints.md).

channel-type.label: Voltage (Phase B-C)
channel-type.description: AC voltage between phases B-C, per MPC Scenario 4 (AC Voltage Phase-Phase, [MPC-041/5]) - see CONCEPT.md §5.4.3. Not populated by this binding: no distinct measurement identifier is available to resolve it (docs/ADR/037-mpc-additional- datapoints.md).

channel-type.label: Voltage (Phase C-A)
channel-type.description: AC voltage between phases C-A, per MPC Scenario 4 (AC Voltage Phase-Phase, [MPC-041/6]) - see CONCEPT.md §5.4.3. Not populated by this binding: no distinct measurement identifier is available to resolve it (docs/ADR/037-mpc-additional- datapoints.md).

channel-type.label: Frequency
channel-type.description: Grid AC frequency, per MPC Scenario 5 (AC Frequency, [MPC-051]) - see CONCEPT.md §5.4.3.

channel-group-type.label: MGCP (Monitoring of Grid Connection Point)
channel-group-type.description: Client-role data read from a trusted device's Entity offering MGCP as a Server actor (Grid Connection Point). Appears once MGCP is detected for this Entity - see docs/ADR/040-mgcp-client-usecase.md.

channel-type.label: Total Active Power
channel-type.description: Total active power at the Grid Connection Point, per MGCP Scenario 2 (Total Active Power, [MGCP-021]). Follows the same load convention MPC's own power Channel already uses ([MPC-001]/[MGCP-001]): positive values are consumption from the grid, negative values are feed-in - see CONCEPT.md §5.4.x.

channel-group-type.label: LPC (Limitation of Power Consumption)
channel-group-type.description: The Controllable System's own currently reported LPC status (Scenario 1) - see CONCEPT.md §5.4.3 and docs/ADR/033-lpc-lpp-limit-duration-channel.md.

channel-group-type.label: LPP (Limitation of Power Production)
channel-group-type.description: The Controllable System's own currently reported LPP status (Scenario 1) - see CONCEPT.md §5.4.3 and docs/ADR/033-lpc-lpp-limit-duration-channel.md.

channel-type.label: Limit Active
channel-type.description: Whether the Entity currently has an active power limit in effect, per Scenario 1 (isLimitActive) - see CONCEPT.md §5.4.3.

channel-type.label: Limit
channel-type.description: The Entity's currently reported power limit value, per Scenario 1 - see CONCEPT.md §5.4.3.

channel-type.label: Limit Duration
channel-type.description: The remaining duration of validity of the currently active power limit (timePeriod.endTime), per Scenario 1 ([LPC-004]) - see CONCEPT.md §5.4.3 and docs/ADR/033-lpc-lpp-limit-duration-channel.md. Per LimitationOfPowerConsumption TS V1.0.0 §3.1.8.2, this SPINE field is a relative duration, not an absolute timestamp - the Channel therefore shows the remaining duration directly, with no further derivation. No state (UNDEF) while absent/removed, meaning the limit is currently unbounded ([LPC-004]).

channel-type.label: Failsafe Limit
channel-type.description: The power limit value the paired Energy Guard has configured to apply if the connection is lost, per Scenario 2 (FailsafeConsumptionActivePowerLimit/ FailsafeProductionActivePowerLimit) - see CONCEPT.md §5.4.3. Read-only: set exclusively by the Energy Guard over EEBus, never from openHAB.

channel-type.label: Failsafe Duration
channel-type.description: The minimum duration the paired Energy Guard has configured for the failsafe limit to remain in effect after a connection loss, per Scenario 2 (FailsafeDurationMinimum) - see CONCEPT.md §5.4.3. Read-only: set exclusively by the Energy Guard over EEBus, never from openHAB.

channel-type.label: Heartbeat
channel-type.description: Fires each time a heartbeat is received from the paired Energy Guard.

channel-type.label: State
channel-type.description: The current state of the Controllable System state machine.

channel-group-type.label: LPC (Limitation of Power Consumption)
channel-group-type.description: Limit commanded by this Energy Guard to its Controllable System partners (Scenario 1). Writable.

channel-group-type.label: LPP (Limitation of Power Production)
channel-group-type.description: Limit commanded by this Energy Guard to its Controllable System partners (Scenario 1). Writable.

channel-type.label: Limit Active
channel-type.description: Whether the limit commanded to the Controllable System partners is active (isLimitActive). Each command sends the combined limit write.

channel-type.label: Limit
channel-type.description: The power limit value commanded to the Controllable System partners. Each command sends the combined limit write.

channel-type.label: Limit Duration
channel-type.description: Duration of validity of the commanded limit (timePeriod.endTime, relative). Not set (never commanded) means the limit is sent unbounded.
